baseline:
B
A sine wave is a continuous, periodic function that extends indefinitely in time, making it spread out. A square pulse, by definition, exists for a finite duration, meaning it is localized or confined to a specific interval in the time domain.

B
The Fourier Transform is a mathematical operation that converts a signal from its representation in the time domain (or spatial domain) into its representation in the frequency domain.

B
This is a manifestation of the Fourier uncertainty principle, which states that a function cannot be highly localized in both the time and frequency domains. There is an inverse relationship: as the spread (variance) of a function in the time domain increases, the spread of its Fourier transform in the frequency domain must decrease.

D
The uncertainty principle states that a signal cannot be localized in both the time and frequency domains simultaneously. As a signal becomes shorter (more localized in time), its corresponding range of frequencies (frequency spread) must become wider.

B
This is a direct consequence of the time-frequency uncertainty principle. To create a signal that is very short in time, it must be composed of a wide range of frequencies. Conversely, a signal with a very narrow frequency band (like a pure tone) must last for a longer duration.
